verdict.rationale: Honeybadger ships an official hosted MCP server (with OAuth) that lets an agent search and filter errors, view occurrences and stack traces, and analyze patterns. A faults API also lists faults per project, so the pull-and-triage half of the story is covered. Filing into a tracker exists only as Honeybadger's own issue export to GitHub, GitLab and Jira, plus rules that create tickets from error events; nothing shows an agent can file a triaged bug through the MCP server or API. missing for 10: documented agent-driven issue creation in a tracker via MCP/API, explicit ranking of 'top' issues, independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can pull my top production issues with stack traces via API or MCP, triage them, and file the real bugs into my tracker

citations.quote: Error investigation: Search and filter errors, view occurrences and stack traces, see affected users, and analyze error patterns.
Our hosted MCP server supports OAuth, so you can connect an agent by approving access in your browser
Returns a list of faults or a single fault for the given project
your issue exports to GitHub or GitLab will contain the full markdown, or the full Jira wiki for JIRA Cloud and JIRA Server
You get to choose which error events result in a notification or ticket being created
